findings.summary: The record file is keyed by taskId only (held/<taskId>.json), but listHeld emits one row per (task, dependency). A task with two non-waiting unmet dependencies A (operator-gated) and B (absent) overwrites the record each time, so the planner gets two lines every tick, breaking the AC-2 once-per-(task, dependency, class) guarantee. Fix: key the record on task and dependency, or hold a list of dependencies in one record. Add a test with a task that has two held dependencies.

findings.summary: A record is never cleared when a hold lifts, so a later hold with the same dependency and class is suppressed by the old notified:true record. Consider deleting the record when the task is no longer held. hierarchyStatus also calls listHeld, which runs loadEligibilityContext on every status call.

findings.summary: triageHeld puts manifest.taskId straight into a file path (held/<taskId>.json) without checking it against TASK_ID_RE, unlike other board modules. Not exploitable today since manifests are written only after id validation, but a TASK_ID_RE.test skip in listHeld would keep a corrupt manifest from writing outside held/.

findings.summary: The held record path held/${taskId}--${dependency}.json is built from two queue-manifest fields that are not validated against TASK_ID_RE. An after entry like ../../../x would resolve outside held/. Not exploitable today since enqueue and the brief parser validate every id before writing a manifest, so only a hand-corrupted queue file could carry a bad value. Hardening: skip a manifest whose taskId or after entry fails TASK_ID_RE in listHeld.
